selected_evidence.summary: The installed schedule passed syntax validation; crond was active and enabled; the exact 02:15 schedule remained installed after reboot.
Initial execution exited 0 and created the requested log. After reboot, the prior line remained and another successful execution increased the log from one to two lines.
The target initially lacked execute permission and contained malformed setup residue. It was repaired, syntax-checked, made executable, and successfully executed after reboot.

Pre-restart boot ID was f38484ef-a289-4d30-9a94-4ab42c44f900; restart was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to e900a354-de54-4a5c-a55c-ba6d80c2ba77. Crond recovered active/enabled, its current-boot startup was recorded, the schedule and existing log persisted, and the command exited 0.

tee /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >/dev/null <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
#!/bin/sh
printf 'inventory maintenance completed at %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ANTRIEB_EOF
chown root:root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance
chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance
/bin/sh -n /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance
stat -c '%A %U:%G %n' /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance
sed -n '1,3p' /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance

tee /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance >/dev/null <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1
ANTRIEB_EOF
chown root:root /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance
chmod 0644 /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance
restorecon /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance 2>/dev/null || true
stat -c '%A %U:%G %n' /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance
cat /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance
crond -T
